title: Rollback executor: idempotency keys + per-tenant throttling for repeated SLO breach events
creator: Benji Okafor
body:
Context
We are adding auto-rollback when latency/error SLOs breach during rollout. This ticket covers the rollback executor safety layer: it must be idempotent under repeated breach events and must throttle rollbacks per tenant (and optionally globally) to avoid cascading changes.

Problem
- SLO evaluator can emit the same breach verdict repeatedly (polling + overlapping windows) and/or multiple monitors can trip for the same rollout.
- Control plane can restart or receive duplicate events.
- Without guardrails, executor can:
  - re-apply the same rollback repeatedly (no-op but noisy + audit spam)
  - oscillate (rollback triggered again while traffic split already reverted)
  - cascade across many tenants during correlated incidents (telemetry issues, region incident)

Goals / requirements
1) Idempotency
- A given breach verdict should cause at most one rollback action per rollout target.
- Duplicate/replayed verdict messages must be safe.
- Executor must be safe across process restarts and leader changes (no reliance on in-memory state).

2) Rate limiting / throttling
- Per-tenant throttling: prevent a single tenant from being rolled back repeatedly within a short period (cooldown is policy-level, but executor should enforce a hard safety throttle as well).
- Provide a global safety limit to avoid triggering rollbacks across too many tenants in a short time window (configurable; can be disabled initially).

3) Safe behavior on repeated breach events
- If already rolled back to the target stable version, treat as idempotent success (no-op) and emit a trace log only (no paging).
- If rollout is already aborted/paused, do not attempt rollback; record a decision trace.
- If verdict is UNKNOWN (monitor stale/unavailable) do not rollback.

4) Auditability
- Emit a single audit event for an actual state change, not for every duplicate verdict.
- Persist enough metadata to understand why a rollback occurred (verdict reason + monitor identity + policy id/version).

Non-goals
- Picking the SLO algorithm (covered by ENG-2314).
- Console history view/pagination (covered by ENG-2316).

Proposed implementation (executor semantics)
A) Idempotency key
We define a stable idempotency key for rollback attempts:
- idempotency_key = sha256("auto_rollback" + tenant_id + route_id + rollout_id + target_stable_version_id + policy_id + policy_version)

Notes:
- Including target_stable_version_id avoids treating different targets as duplicates.
- Including policy_version avoids collisions if policy changes mid-rollout.
- We intentionally do NOT include window_end timestamp to prevent repeated rollbacks due to shifting windows.

B) Persistent idempotency record
Add a small state record in rollout-controller storage (same persistence layer as rollout state) keyed by idempotency_key:
- created_at
- last_attempt_at
- status: STARTED | APPLIED | SKIPPED_NOOP | FAILED
- applied_rollout_state_version (optimistic concurrency token)
- verdict_summary (short string) + monitor_identity

Executor flow:
1. Validate verdict is actionable:
   - verdict == BREACH
   - rollout_state is active AND has a prior stable version
   - traffic split currently sends >0% to candidate OR rollout is in canary/ab state
2. Throttle checks:
   - Per-tenant throttle: if tenant had any APPLIED rollback in last X minutes (hard safety), SKIP with reason THROTTLED_TENANT.
   - Global throttle (optional, behind flag): if >N rollbacks in last Y minutes, SKIP with reason THROTTLED_GLOBAL.
3. Acquire idempotency record:
   - create-if-not-exists; if exists and status in {APPLIED, SKIPPED_NOOP} => return idempotent success.
   - if exists and status STARTED but last_attempt_at < now-lease => treat as recoverable and continue (handles crash mid-execution).
4. Apply rollback with CAS:
   - update routing config / rollout state using optimistic concurrency; ensure we only revert to prior stable version.
   - set split back to 100% stable (or previous stable split depending on rollout type).
   - mark rollout as "aborted_by_policy" with reason="AUTO_ROLLBACK_SLO_BREACH".
5. Mark idempotency record APPLIED and emit:
   - audit event: rollout.auto_rollback.executed
   - incident-bot notification (Slack) with links

C) No-op detection
If traffic split is already 100% stable OR candidate is not receiving traffic:
- mark idempotency record SKIPPED_NOOP
- emit decision trace metric but do not page.

D) Metrics / observability (executor-owned)
- rollout_controller.rollback_executor.attempts_total{result=applied|noop|throttled|failed}
- rollout_controller.rollback_executor.idempotency_cache_hits_total
- rollout_controller.rollback_executor.throttle_denied_total{scope=tenant|global}
- rollout_controller.rollback_executor.cas_conflicts_total

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Duplicate breach verdicts result in at most one applied rollback.
- [x] Executor is safe under restarts; repeated execution attempts converge to correct end state.
- [x] Per-tenant throttle prevents repeated rollbacks within hard safety window (default: 15m; configurable).
- [x] Audit events are emitted once per applied rollback and include policy id/version + monitor identity.
- [x] Integration tests cover: duplicate events, CAS conflict, no-op case, throttle deny.

Implementation notes / decisions
- Hard safety throttle is separate from policy cooldown. Policy cooldown is evaluated upstream; executor throttle is a last line of defense.
- We will ship global throttle behind a feature flag initially (to tune based on game day + real traffic).

Links
- Design context: Auto-rollback SLO integration design spec (Confluence)
- PR (main): sources/github/redwood/pr-18471.json
- Follow-up guardrail (unknown/stale monitors): sources/github/redwood/pr-18546.json
- Related: ENG-2314 (evaluator), ENG-2317 (audit events), ENG-2318 (metrics)

Test plan
- Unit tests:
  - idempotency key stability
  - record create/update transitions
  - tenant throttle window logic
- Integration tests (synthetic harness):
  - send same breach verdict 10x concurrently -> 1 rollback applied
  - simulate process restart mid-execution -> eventual APPLIED and stable routing
  - CAS conflict (rollout state changed concurrently) -> retry + eventual consistency
  - throttle denial -> no routing change + metrics increment

Rollout / risk
- Enable executor behind feature flag: rollout.auto_rollback_executor_enabled
- Start with internal canaries only, then low-risk tenants.
- Monitor: cas_conflicts, throttled_total, and audit event volume.

Open questions
- Do we want to include region in idempotency key? (Current plan: rollout_id already binds to region-scoped rollout; confirm with Mina/Ravi.)
- What is the initial hard throttle window per tenant? Proposal: 15m. SRE input requested.
comments: 2025-02-07 (Miles Thornton): +1 on separate hard safety throttle from policy cooldown. During correlated incidents, policy evaluation can still be noisy; executor must be conservative. Please also ensure no rollback on UNKNOWN verdicts (monitor outage).
2025-02-08 (Jordan Lee): For idempotency key, include policy_version; we’ve seen config edits mid-rollout. Also recommend treating APPLIED as terminal to avoid audit spam.
2025-02-10 (Mina Haddad): Routing write path uses CAS; please count CAS conflicts and avoid infinite retry loops. Cap retries and emit reason.

2025-02-12 (Rafael Mendes): For oncall, no-op should not page. Applied rollbacks should page only for Dedicated/Enterprise tiers; others can be ticket. (Paging policy tracked elsewhere but executor should set appropriate event type/metadata.)
2025-02-18 (Benji Okafor): Implemented idempotency record + per-tenant throttle. Global throttle behind flag. Added no-op detection when stable already at 100%. Draft PR up for review.
2025-02-20 (Allison Grant): Please attach monitor identity (route/model/region/tier) in the decision trace. We’ll need it for dashboards and false-positive analysis.

2025-02-24 (Benji Okafor): PR merged. Added metrics + CAS conflict counter; decision trace logs include monitor identity + policy id/version. Follow-up PR to handle UNKNOWN verdict from stale monitor merged separately.
